Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Foundation and Vision

The Conservative Party presents itself as the guardian of economic stability, having navigated Britain through Covid and the Ukraine-related energy crisis. With inflation down from 11.1% to 2.3%, real wages rising, and the UK economy outperforming Germany, France, Italy, and the United States, the manifesto argues that abandoning this proven approach would return Britain to "square one" under Labour—characterised by unfunded spending, higher taxes, and mounting debt.

## Tax Cuts for Working People and Pensioners

Central to the manifesto is a commitment to halve employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, delivering £1,350 in savings for average workers. Self-employed individuals will see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees pensioners that both the State Pension and their tax-free allowance will rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, preventing the State Pension from being dragged into income tax.

## Supporting Families and Reforming Welfare

The manifesto promises 30 hours of free childcare weekly for working parents with children from nine months old, saving families approximately £6,900 annually. Child Benefit reforms will shift to a household basis, protecting families until combined income reaches £120,000. The welfare system will undergo significant reform, saving £12 billion annually through tighter disability benefit assessments, reformed fit note processes, and stricter sanctions for those refusing suitable employment after 12 months.

## Border Security and Immigration Control

Immigration is deemed "too high," with the Conservatives pledging a legally binding, annually-falling cap on migration. The Rwanda deportation scheme will operate with monthly flights to deter illegal crossings. International asylum rules will be reformed through diplomatic efforts, and visa fees will increase while access will be restricted from countries not cooperating on migration priorities.

## National Security and Defence

Defence spending will reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030—the largest strengthening since the Cold War. The manifesto commits to maintaining the Trident nuclear deterrent, supporting Ukraine "for the long haul," and establishing a National Defence and Resilience Plan. A new Veterans' Bill will enshrine veterans' rights in law.

## NHS and Public Services

NHS spending will increase above inflation each year, with 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors by Parliament's end. A £3.4 billion technology investment will transform services, while Pharmacy First expansion and 50 new Community Diagnostic Centres will bring care closer to patients. The Cass Review's recommendations on gender-questioning children will be fully implemented.

## Young People and Education

Mandatory National Service will be introduced for all 18-year-olds, offering either competitive military placements or community service roles. The Advanced British Standard will transform 16-19 education, ending the "artificial divide" between academic and technical learning. Mobile phones will be banned during school hours by statutory requirement.

## Net Zero and Energy

The manifesto maintains commitment to net zero by 2050 but through a "pragmatic and proportionate" approach. Annual oil and gas licensing rounds will continue, green levies on household bills will be kept lower than 2023 levels, and no new green levies will be introduced. Nuclear power will be expanded through Small Modular Reactors, while onshore wind development will require local democratic consent.

## Housing and Communities

The target is 1.6 million homes in England, built primarily through brownfield development and urban densification rather than on Green Belt land. First-time buyers will see Stamp Duty permanently abolished on properties up to £425,000, with a new Help to Buy scheme requiring only 5% deposits. The Equality Act will be clarified to define sex as biological sex, protecting single-sex spaces.

## Protecting British Values

The manifesto positions itself firmly against "divisive identity politics" and gender ideology, promising to protect female-only spaces in healthcare and sport. Parents will have rights to see what children are taught, particularly on sensitive matters. The document emphasises national pride, heritage protection, and maintaining British values against extremism.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

**The Central Promise: Change and National Renewal**

This manifesto presents Labour as the antidote to fourteen years of Conservative "chaos" that has damaged British families' finances, left the country vulnerable internationally, and eroded trust in politics. Labour's core argument is that sustainable growth requires partnership between government, business, and communities—rejecting the Conservative approach of market fundamentalism that culminated in the disastrous mini-budget.

**Foundations: Security, Borders, and Economic Stability**

Labour positions itself as the party of fiscal responsibility, committing to strict rules: balancing day-to-day spending with revenues, and reducing debt as a share of GDP. They pledge no increases to Income Tax, National Insurance, or VAT for working people, while closing loopholes for non-doms and private equity. On borders, Labour will scrap the Rwanda scheme, create a Border Security Command to tackle smuggling gangs, and clear the asylum backlog. Defence commitments include unwavering NATO support, maintaining the nuclear deterrent, and conducting a Strategic Defence Review.

**Five National Missions**

*Economic Growth*: Labour will establish an Industrial Strategy Council, create a National Wealth Fund with £7.3 billion, and reform planning to build 1.5 million homes. They promise to cap corporation tax at 25%, support small businesses, and devolve power to regions through Combined Authorities.

*Clean Energy Superpower*: Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, will partner with industry to deliver clean power by 2030. The manifesto promises 650,000 green jobs, the Warm Homes Plan to upgrade five million homes, and maintaining existing North Sea licences while issuing no new exploration licences.

*Taking Back Our Streets*: Labour pledges to halve knife crime within a decade, introduce a Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands of new officers, create Young Futures hubs, and halve violence against women and girls through specialist rape courts and domestic abuse experts in 999 control rooms.

*Breaking Down Barriers to Opportunity*: The party will recruit 6,500 new teachers, establish free breakfast clubs in every primary school, create 3,000 new nursery places in primary schools, reform apprenticeships through a Growth and Skills Levy, and develop a child poverty reduction strategy.

*NHS Fit for the Future*: Commitments include 40,000 extra appointments weekly, doubling CT and MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health professionals, and shifting toward prevention and community-based care through Neighbourhood Health Centres.

**Workers' Rights and Devolution**

Labour's New Deal for Working People promises legislation within 100 days to ban exploitative zero-hour contracts, end fire-and-rehire practices, and establish day-one employment rights. They will create a genuine living wage by reforming the Low Pay Commission's remit.

Devolution features prominently, with new powers for Combined Authorities, statutory Local Growth Plans, and a reset of relationships with Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland through a Council of the Nations and Regions.

**Democratic Renewal**

The manifesto addresses political integrity through an Ethics and Integrity Commission, banning MPs from paid advisory roles, removing hereditary peers, introducing Lords retirement at 80, and extending voting rights to 16-17 year-olds.

**International Outlook**

Labour commits to remaining outside the EU while seeking improved trade relationships, a veterinary agreement, and a new UK-EU security pact. They pledge steadfast Ukraine support, continued AUKUS commitment, and restoring 0.7% aid spending when fiscally possible. Recognition of Palestinian statehood is promised as contribution to a two-state solution.

**Ideological Core**

Throughout, Labour frames its vision as restoring the promise that hard work leads to success regardless of background—contrasting "securonomics" against Conservative ideology that gifts growth "from the few to the many." This is positioned not as radical change but as common-sense patriotism: serving working people, embracing business partnership, and rebuilding national confidence through competent, stable governance.
